page.layout: One column of running text, full width. No marginal notes or footnotes. Running head at the top with the page number to its left.

main_text.p: sed hæc licet homini ministrent, & nos adiuuent cooperando nobiscum, irrationabilia tamen sunt; & homine longe inferiora, neq; illi similia vel substantia, vel dignitate.

Deinde non fuisset Adæ bonum vt solus maneret, quia non fuisset ei iucundum, cum nullum confabulatorem haberet: est autem homo animal sociabile, vt ille ait: adeo vt etiam in coelo nullus cupiat esse solus. vnde quidam vetus Hebræus: Aut societas, aut mors. Et Cicero: Solem è mundo tollere videntur, qui tollunt amicitiam. Et alius Hebræus [?] Id est, Cuicunque non est vxor, is non est homo. Et Mimnermus: [?] q. d. vitam non esse vitam sine dulci coniugio. Item Philippus, [?] Id est,
Dulce merum, dulcis coniunx; mens conscia recti: Nil tribus his cunctis dulcius esse potest.

Præterea nō fuisset bonū homine mansisse[?] solū. Si enim hoc factū fuisset, vnde nancisci potuissemus Immanuele, qui feinen mulieris exiftit benefices nos? imo, quomodo potuissemus nos omnes nasci? Nonne enim mulieres genuerunt regè, & omnem populū, qui dominatur mari & terræ, & ex illis nati sunt, & ipsæ educauerunt eos, qui plantauerunt vineas, ex quib. vinū fit: & ipsæ faciunt stolas omnium hominū, & ipsæ faciunt gloriam

page.notes: Printed "fuisset" and similar long-s forms are rendered with plain s. "Immanuele" and "feinen mulieris exiftit benefices" are as printed and doubtful in places. The Hebrew line after "Et alius Hebræus" is marked [?] because the letters are hard to read at this resolution; the Greek of Mimnermus and Philippus is also uncertain and marked [?] throughout. "mansisse" is a best guess for the printed word, marked [?]. The printed line "gloriam" is followed on the next line by a catchword-like word "riam", which is the end of the word "gloriam" carried to the foot of the page and is treated as its continuation; no separate catchword is given. A line is underlined across "adeo vt etiam in coelo nullus cupiat esse solus", which is likely a later mark and was not transcribed as text. Some Greek accents and breathings may be misread.
